notes: §1985:XIV.3.2.4 GR2: the disconnection comes "at the earliest time the source or destination is inactive", and DISABLE "will never cause the remaining portion of the message to be terminated during transmission to or from a terminal"; §1985:XIV.3.6.4 GR6: "the MCS will not transmit any portion of a message to a communication device until the entire message has been released to the MCS". A partial message lives in MessageControlSession's Dialogue, not in the store: #Receive serves a pending remainder before any enabled check, and a portion released before DISABLE stays held and completes after ENABLE. Probes at --std 85: input and I-O RECEIVE remainders continued after DISABLE INPUT and DISABLE I-O TERMINAL; OUTPUT partial, DISABLE, EMI gave 10 with key 2 and HELLOHELLO reached D1.out on ENABLE; I-O partial, DISABLE, EMI gave 10 and the whole HELLOHELLO reached TT.out after ENABLE.

next.reason: 1985: "the execution of a DISABLE statement will cause the logical disconnection at the earliest time the source or destination is inactive"; 2023: "No 2023 clause holds the DISABLE statement; the 2023 SEND/RECEIVE rules use a message server, with no enable/disable". No 2023 clause holds the DISABLE feature. The 2023 communication candidates (SEND, RECEIVE) use a message server and have no DISABLE statement, so the 1985 rule is dropped.
